name: site-footer
description: The end of the page, and the answer to "a page ends on purpose". One slot and no parts previously, while the real footer carried a brand block, three separate link groups each with its own heading, and a legal line — assembled by hand in one component. Three `<nav>` elements is correct and needs three labels; without them a screen reader hears "navigation" three times and cannot tell which is which.

groups.$description: `auto-fit` with a `minmax` floor rather than a column count, so three groups become two and then one without a breakpoint per step.

group-title.$description: Composes `text--eyebrow`. Only the colour is this unit's; the size, weight, case and tracking come from the one definition.

meta.$description: The legal line. Wraps to a column on a narrow viewport rather than shrinking a copyright notice past its own words.

page.$description: For a surface whose page is already dark, where a marine footer would vanish into it.

a11y.note: Each link group is its own `<nav>` with its own `aria-label` — "Product", "Legal", "Social" — because three unlabelled navigation landmarks in one footer tell a screen-reader user nothing about which is which. The footer is a `contentinfo` landmark by virtue of being a top-level `<footer>`, and stops being one if it is nested inside a `<section>`.
